title: Lian, Batangas residents evacuated due to 'habagat'
content_lead: LIAN, Batangas - One hundred four individuals from flood-prone areas here were assisted by Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) Sub-Station (CGSS)- Lian in the pre-emptive evacuation conducted in Sitio Aplaya, Brgy. Balibago, due to the effects of a low-pressure area (LPA) and the intensified southwest monsoon, or "habagat", on Tuesday, August 18. CGSS Lian coordinated with the officials of Barangay Balibago and safely transported the evacuated residents to the Balibago Elementary School, the designated evacuation center. The evacuees were safely evacuated and are currently staying at the evacuation center. CGSS Lian continues to monitor the situation and coordinate with relevant agencies and the local government unit (LGU). The PCG also reminded residents in flood-prone areas to evacuate immediately and heed local government advisories should weather conditions worsen. While the Coast Guard Sub-Station (CGSS) Lemery, in coordination with the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO) San Luis, Batangas, conducted a clearing and debris removal operation at Brgy. Poblacion, Purok 6, San Luis, on Aug. 18 following the effects of the enhanced Southwest Monsoon. Upon arrival, the team found a fallen tree and accumulated debris obstructing the waterway and drainage canal, causing muddy rainwater to accumulate and posing a potential flooding risk to nearby residential areas. The team removed the fallen branches and debris to restore the flow of water and mitigate the risk of flooding. CGSS Lemery continues to coordinate with concerned agencies and barangay officials and monitor the area for further incidents within its area of responsibility. (AOR)

title: Cavite eyes relocation of 1,300 coastal families after storm surge
content_lead: A storm surge inundated coastal communities in Tanza, Cavite due to the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat, sending floodwaters into homes and forcing residents to evacuate. According to a "24 Oras" report by Jonathan Andal, the local government said it is considering relocating around 1,300 families from 13 coastal barangays in the province starting next year. The families will be provided with free housing, the report said. The storm surge in Barangay Halayhay damaged homes and left furniture, beds, kitchen equipment and other belongings submerged or destroyed. The sandbags lined up by residents along the coast proved no match for the waves that rose higher than the roofs of homes. Melanie Blanco recalled being struck by a piece of wood as floodwaters entered her home. "Dapat wala nang tao sa tabing-dagat. Iyong iba naman nabigyan ng pabahay kaso ang naging problem, bumalik-balik dyan, binenta nila ang bahay," Tanza Mayor Archangel Matro said. "Pag nailikas namin sila, sisiguraduhin namin na hindi na sila babalik doon." (There should no longer be anyone living along the shoreline. Some of them were given housing, but the problem is that they kept returning there and sold the houses. Once we relocate them, we will make sure they do not return there.) A resident, Rowena Bagtas, said relocation would take them away from their source of livelihood. Cavite Governor Abeng Remulla said the local government could arrange for free transportation to take them to their place of work. The victims of the storm surge appealed for materials to reconstruct their homes as well as food and clothes. GMA Kapuso Foundation provided relief packs to the affected families. In Barangay Medicion in Imus, Cavite, floodwaters reached above head level. The Cavite Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office said around 25 percent of Imus was submerged in floodwaters.

title: 'Laid-off' workers turn to side jobs to survive
content_lead: LAGUNA, Philippines - From 6 am to 6 pm, six days a week, Dante Cantos, 55, has worked at San Miguel Integrated Logistics Services Inc. (SMILSI) as a forklift operator for about a year and a half. Before working at SMILSI, he worked for another company that closed down. He was among the hundreds of workers who were recently put on "floating status" by SMILSI. Julius Sarsuela, 39, had also been with the company for nearly three years as a reach truck operator, often working the same hours and days as Cantos. He was required to work off-shifts, particularly during inventory periods when operators like him were needed. Like Cantos, Sarsuela was among the workers affected by the move. Both of them are among the SMILSI workers who have joined the picket line in front of San Miguel Corporation's (SMC) Sta. Rosa Industrial Complex in Santa Rosa, Laguna after some workers said they were dismissed, or "tinanggal," without prior notice. The dispute came just a few months after workers under the Unyon ng mga Manggagawa sa San Miguel Logistics-Independent (USMILSI-IND) earned collective bargaining rights. About 800 SMILSI workers were prevented from reporting to their posts starting July 6, after the company placed them under floating status without certainty over their wages, benefits, or arrangements for returning to work. The company defended the move, after it lost a bidding process for its warehouse, transport, and bundling operations, as previously reported by Bulatlat. SMILSI is a subsidiary of San Miguel Corporation, created to "provide effective and efficient logistics and warehousing solutions to the San Miguel group of companies." We reached out to SMC's Media Affairs and Communications teams via text and through multiple email channels, including its legal, customer care, shareholder services and assistance, and whistleblower offices, on August 5, 10, and 12.

title: PBBM brings 'Bawat Bayan Makikinabang' program in Lucena City
content_lead: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Tuesday led the "Bawat Bayan Makikinabang" program in Lucena City, Quezon, highlighting the administration's commitment to ensuring that government programs reach communities across the country through strengthened support to local government units (LGUs). Around 4,000 of the total 52,439 beneficiaries from vulnerable sectors and indigent families across Lucena City's 33 barangays each received 10-kilo sacks of rice under the first tranche of Bagong Pilipinas Rice Program. Funded through the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF), the program provides rice assistance to vulnerable households every two months while boosting local agriculture by allowing LGUs to directly purchase good-quality "palay" from local farmers and cooperatives. About 165 Bagong Pilipinas Presidential Scholars also received P20,000 from the administration under the Socio-Civic Projects Fund (SCPF), where every barangay gets P200,000 to fund the education needs of scholars as well as the priority programs and projects in their respective communities. As of July 17, 2026, the SCPF-Bawat Barangay Makikinabang Program has released an allocation totaling P6.97 billion to 34,830 barangays, according to the Presidential Communications Office. In his speech at the Lucena Convention Center, President Marcos Jr. underscored the need to intensify support to graduating students as they tend to pause or stop their studies due to financial constraints. "Kaya ito ang ginagawa natin ay bibigyan natin ng mga iskolar ng P20,000 at para gamitin ninyo sa inyong pag-aaral, sa pagtulong sa inyong mga sarili, kung ano man ang pangangailangan ninyo," he said. "Ang aking lang advice na binibigay, pagnakakausap po ang ating mga presidential scholar, ang aking ko lang binibigay na advice, sana ay mapakinabangan ninyo na mabuti itong tulong na ibinibigay ng Office of the President," he added.

title: Red Cross rescues 6 amid flooding in Rizal's low-lying areas
content_lead: The rescued individuals were brought to the evacuation center by a rescue boat. Some low-lying areas in Rizal Province were not spared as the heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat caused flooding. According to Emil Sumangil's report in "24 Oras" on Monday, personnel from the Philippine Red Cross waded through waist-deep floodwaters, along with the strong winds and rain, to rescue six people in a household in Rodriguez, Rizal early morning. The rescued individuals were brought to the evacuation center by a rescue boat. In Barangay Burgos, also in Rodriguez, the floodwater was chest-deep after a nearby river overflowed. "Last night, around 11 p.m., the water was already going down. This morning, around 5 or 6, it started rising again because the rain poured heavily again early this morning," said Barangay Kagawad JR Simbulan. The barangay cleared the tree trunks and waste to help the floodwater to recede. In San Mateo, residents were stranded after several roads became impassable due to flooding. The floodwater at Barangay Malanday was knee-deep at noon. Although the weather slightly improved, the flood was still an inconvenience for many. For instance, the flood caused traffic along Felix Avenue. But things were worse near Marcos Highway in Antipolo City as a subdivision became impassable for vehicles. A resident had to use a jetski to traverse within their community. Not everyone are fortunate to have such a water vehicle. Many residents had no choice but to wade through the floodwaters to do their errands. They argued that paying for a boat o pedicab ride would be unreasonable. "It's not that cheap. They were asking for P100 for a ride. If I don't have any wounds, I will just wade through the waters," one man said. Delivery riders were also affected by the flooding. "My booking was suddenly cancelled...I did not expect it to be that deep," said rider Arnold Oliveras, noting that it was his supposedly first booking for the day.

She was forced to evacuate with her grandchildren after floodwaters quickly rose in their community due to the heavy rains. Six years after Typhoon Ulyses struck Montalban, Thelma found herself reliving the trauma as the recent rains brought back memories of the devastating floods. With no available transportation, Thelma immediately carried her grandchild to safety and evacuated with her six grandchildren. "I didn't know where my grandchildren could get a ride because the water suddenly rose. I had to make sacrifices to make sure my grandchildren would be safe," she said. They remain at an evacuation center as they wait for the floodwaters to subside. Whenever the weather improves, Thelma and her husband return to their home to clean up. "Hopefully, the flooding in our area can be prevented. I hope the drainage systems can be fixed because some of them are still clogged." title: 70 families evacuated as rains batter Taytay, Rizal
content_lead: LUCENA CITY - Residents of low-lying and flood-prone areas in Taytay, Rizal were enjoined by the municipal government on Saturday to take immediate safety measures amid continuous rains triggered by the southwest monsoon or "habagat." As of 1 p.m., at least 70 families, or 240 individuals, from the barangays of Muzon, Dolores and San Juan were evacuated and were temporarily staying at evacuation centers, the municipal Public Information Office (PIO) said. "Do not wait for the situation to worsen before evacuating. Put the safety of your family first, especially children, senior citizens, pregnant women, persons with disabilities (PWDs), and those with medical conditions," the municipal PIO said in an advisory in Filipino. The municipal government continues to monitor the situation and prepare for the safety of residents affected by the persistent rains and rising water levels. The Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO), together with other concerned municipal offices, are closely monitoring conditions in various areas and remains on standby to respond to the needs of affected residents. Authorities reminded residents to remain alert, follow official advisories, and evacuate early if conditions in their areas become unsafe.

title: DAR distributes P5.49M in farm machinery to Calabarzon beneficiaries
content_lead: THE Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) on Sunday said it distributed P5.49 million worth of farm machinery and equipment to beneficiaries and farmer organizations in the provinces of Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, and Quezon (Calabarzon). DAR Undersecretary for Field Operations Kazel Celeste led the turnover on July 21 in Lucena. The distribution was part of DAR's agrarian reform program, which also included the awarding of certificates of land ownership, certificates of condonation and release of mortgage, and electronic titles under the Support to Parcelization of Lands for Individual Titling project. Batangas received P1.98 million worth of equipment, including a 40-horsepower, four-wheel-drive tractor with rotary tiller and disc plow, three motorcycles with carriers, weighing scales and powered pressure washers. Cavite got a 50-horsepower, four-wheel tractor worth P1.47 million. Quezon I was given a motorcycle with sidecar and a hand tractor worth P300,000, while Quezon II received a multi-tiller, ride-on mini combine harvester, mechanical rice transplanter, grass cutters and knapsack sprayers worth P1.75 million.
